articles.summary: Accomplished global manufacturing executive will lead the expansion of FuelCell Energy’s manufacturing operations and build the systems required to support future growth. DANBURY, Conn., Oct. 12, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) - FuelCell Energy, Inc. (Nasdaq: FCEL) today announced that John Dansby has joined the company as Senior Vice President, Scale Up Manufacturing. He will lead FuelCell Energy’s manufacturing scale-up strategy, including expanding its Torrington, Conn., operations to support 500 megawatts (MW) of annual capacity and developing the manufacturing systems and capabilities needed for growth beyond 500 MW. The appointment comes as FuelCell Energy is scaling manufacturing to meet customers’ growing need for reliable, distributed power that can be deployed quickly. Dansby brings more than two decades of leadership across complex, high-volume global manufacturing operations. articles.title: FuelCell Energy Appoints John Dansby to Lead Manufacturing Scale-Up

articles.summary: Matthew Latino appointed CFO; Michael Bishop to continue as senior advisor DANBURY, Conn., Oct. 07, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) - FuelCell Energy, Inc. (Nasdaq: FCEL) today announced that Michael Bishop will transition from his role as Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer of the Company. Matthew Latino will succeed him as Executive Vice President, Chief Financial Officer and Treasurer effective October 7, 2026, as part of a planned transition. Bishop, who has served as the Company’s CFO for 15 years during an overall tenure with the Company of more than two decades, will remain with FuelCell Energy as a senior advisor through the Company’s 2027 Annual Meeting of Stockholders to support continuity and the transition. articles.title: FuelCell Energy Announces Chief Financial Officer Transition

articles.summary: Financing underscores continued U.S. support for American manufacturing and clean energy exports DANBURY, Conn., Oct. 29, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) - FuelCell Energy, Inc. (Nasdaq: FCEL) today announced the completion of the second tranche of its previously announced $49 million financing supported by the Export-Import Bank of the United States (EXIM). The approximately $24.7 million balance (before closing and transaction fees) completes the financing package approved by EXIM in June 2026. The financing supports FuelCell Energy’s delivery of five 2.8-megawatt (MW) FuelCell Energy Blocks to Gyeonggi Green Energy (GGE) in South Korea. With nearly 60 MW of installed capacity, the GGE site is among the largest fuel cell installations in the world, has been in continuous operations for 13 years, and demonstrates FuelCell Energy’s long-standing experience delivering distributed, utility-scale power solutions. articles.summary: Digital infrastructure executive brings data center, investment and transaction expertise as FuelCell Energy advances its power strategy for AI and advanced computing DANBURY, Conn., Oct. 28, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) - FuelCell Energy, Inc. (Nasdaq: FCEL) today announced the appointment of Peter Hopper to its board of directors, adding deep digital infrastructure and investment expertise as the company advances its strategy to provide reliable power for data centers. Hopper brings more than 25 years of experience across data centers, digital infrastructure, private equity, investment banking, capital formation and MA. He is co-founder and managing director of Primary Digital Infrastructure, where he advises and invests across data centers, connectivity, cloud, power and AI-related infrastructure. Previously, as a managing director at DigitalBridge, he co-led the approximately $11 billion take-private acquisition of Switch, Inc. and co-headed its $2.4 billion Strategic Asset Fund.
articles.title: FuelCell Energy Appoints Peter Hopper to Board of Directors as it Advances Data Center Power Strategy

articles.summary: PJM assessment recognizes nearly all of FuelCell Energy’s installed capacity as dependable, an important proof point for reliability and potential capacity-market economics. DANBURY, Conn., Oct. 21, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) - FuelCell Energy, Inc. (Nasdaq: FCEL) announced that its FuelCell Energy Block System received a 99.873% rating in PJM Interconnection’s unit-specific Effective Load Carrying Capability (ELCC) assessment conducted as part of PJM’s 2028/29 Reliability Backstop Procurement (RBP) process. The result indicates that PJM may recognize nearly all of FuelCell Energy’s evaluated system’s capacity as dependable, providing an important measure of reliability for customers evaluating on-site power and informing potential participation in PJM’s capacity market. Rapid data center growth is driving electricity demand and sharpening the focus on how large loads secure power. PJM projects 32 GW of peak load growth across its region from 2024 to 2030, with approximately 30 GW expected
articles.title: FuelCell Energy Block System Receives 99.873% PJM Capacity Rating as Demand Grows for On-Site Power
